Only devices whose USB name says FM-1 (or a firmware on it) are asked.

FM-1s sold since autumn 2026 have a newer flash chip (0xB36014). A firmware that knows only the first one (0x856014) keeps your saves in RAM there, and updates from it may fail. The FM-1 cannot tell the app: say which one yours has, if you know.

M-VAVE\'s V15, unchanged, from M-VAVE\'s own repository (fm1_open, Apache-2.0), checked against its sha256.
If the FM-1 does not start: hold OCT− and OCT+ for 5 s (the chip\'s boot mode), or see thefirmwarehub.com/tools/rescue.
Do not unplug the FM-1 or leave the app while it writes.

The firmware\'s own C code, compiled to WebAssembly and built into the app: it plays offline, with the phone\'s speaker or headphones.
%1$d other firmwares play in the browser
The others are their makers\' own pages: they need the internet.

An emulator of the M-VAVE FM-1 for Android: the firmwares themselves, their update packages unchanged, on an emulated FM-1, played with your fingers, a MIDI keyboard or a controller; offline once downloaded. And The Firmware Hub\'s list, the makers\' browser versions, and installing on a real FM-1 over USB.

Firmware list: The Firmware Hub – thefirmwarehub.com, under %1$s. Read at most once a day; shown unchanged, filtered and sorted on the phone. Each card\'s text and picture belong to its maker (from their fmhub.json and repository).

Each belongs to its maker, under its own licence (mostly GPL-3.0 or MPL-2.0): the card names it and links the source at the release\'s tag. Packages come from the makers\' GitHub releases, never from the hub, and are installed only if their sha256 is the one the hub checked.

FM-1 Pocket is free software under the GPL-3.0: the panel, the sound and MIDI around the emulator, the list, the downloads and the installer. Not made by or affiliated with M-VAVE, The Firmware Hub or fm1-emu\'s author.
M-VAVE and FM-1 are trademarks of their owners.
Unofficial firmware, free and without warranty: you install it at your own risk. Back up your projects first.
Play it from a MIDI keyboard
A keyboard on the phone plays the FM-1 (notes, wheels, controllers; not SysEx). On USB both need an OTG hub; a Bluetooth keyboard Android knows works too. In Play, the keyboard plays the simulators.
The keyboard or the FM-1 would not open (another app using it?).
A MIDI keyboard on the phone (USB through an OTG hub, or Bluetooth) plays the simulators: switch the simulator on and play.

The firmware itself, its C code built for the phone: its screen, the knobs (drag up or down), the buttons and the 27 keys, played with your fingers, a MIDI keyboard or a controller\'s knobs (MIDI learn). Its presets and settings are kept.
No MIDI input: connect a keyboard (USB through an OTG hub, or Bluetooth)
A controller\'s knob (a MIDI CC) can turn one of the panel\'s: touch Learn, then move the controller\'s knob. The other CCs, the notes, the wheels and pressure go to the firmware as from USB.
Move a knob on the controller for %1$s (touch here to stop)
The firmware\'s memory on the phone (your presets, its settings):

The firmware itself, its update package (.fwsc) unchanged, on an emulated FM-1: its two cores, screen, keys, knobs and sound (fm1-emu by Joakim Eriksson). Offline: what is on the phone plays without the internet. Each firmware keeps its own presets and settings.
More: in Firmwares, a firmware\'s page, Play in the emulator (it downloads once, then plays offline).
The emulated FM-1 stopped (the firmware did something the emulator does not have yet).
Download and play in the emulator
The emulation is fm1-emu, by Joakim Eriksson (MIT): the FM-1\'s cores, screen, keys, knobs and sound.

The emulator itself: the FM-1\'s two JieLi cores (their instruction set, compiled to native code), the chip around them, the screen, the keys and knobs, the flash, MIDI IN and the audio. This app builds its library (fm1-web, v0.5.1) for Android unchanged.
Each firmware\'s maker, named on its card
The update protocol the installer speaks (fm1_install.py), and the base most FM-1 firmwares are built on. GPL-3.0.
In the app (it plays with no download). On Felucca and on Hortator by DEADACTIVE. GPL-3.0.
A firmware not on the hub (yet): its repository on GitHub. Its newest release with a .fwsc is downloaded, then plays offline; new releases come by themselves.
Nobody checked it: no identity, loader or sha256 check of the hub. It plays in the emulator as it is; on a real FM-1 only with an update loader.
That is not a GitHub repository (owner/repo).
